reviews.vuln_type: Path Traversal to Arbitrary File Read with Second-Order Cloud Exfiltration
reviews.minimum_role_capability: authenticated user with edit_theme_options; most relevant on multisite site-admin contexts
reviews.reason: The local path-to-read primitive is still visible in code, but the claimed attacker-visible impact remains second-order because the ZIP is only posted to Kubio cloud and the repository does not show successful retrieval with an attacker-controlled API key. The gate's line mismatch is real: line 282 is the file read, while the named sink function kubio_create_snippet_zip starts at line 237.

counter_evidence.detail: /snippet is not public; its permission_callback requires current_user_can('edit_theme_options').
/kubio-api-key POST is gated by the same current_user_can('edit_theme_options') boundary, so the API-key write stays in the same trust zone as /snippet.
The outbound upload target is built with Utils::getSnippetsURL('/save'), so the remote host is fixed by plugin constants rather than attacker input.

missing_evidence: Need an end-to-end capture showing that a forged uploads URL with '/../' survives the normal snippet serialization path and reaches kubio_create_snippet_zip unchanged.
Need proof that an attacker-controlled Kubio cloud API key set through /kubio-api-key is accepted for snippet uploads and lets the same actor retrieve the uploaded ZIP.
Need either an intercepted outbound ZIP or a downloaded cloud artifact proving that a sensitive local file such as wp-config.php was actually embedded.
dynamic_test_plan: Step 1: Log in as a user who really passes current_user_can('edit_theme_options') on the target site, obtain a valid REST nonce for that session, and POST /wp-json/kubio/v1/kubio-api-key with JSON {"key":"<attacker-controlled valid Kubio cloud key>"}.

Step 2: Reuse the same cookies and X-WP-Nonce header to POST /wp-json/kubio/v1/snippet with a legitimate captured snippet body, but replace one media URL inside snippet JSON with https://<target-host>/wp-content/uploads/../../wp-config.php and keep a valid data:image screenshot payload.

Step 3: Intercept or retrieve the resulting upload to https://cloud.kubiobuilder.com/api/snippets/save and inspect the ZIP for the target file contents; if cloud retrieval is unavailable, instrument pre_http_request or a DNS/hosts override to capture the outgoing binary body locally.

reviews.vuln_type: Insufficient Capability Check for Plugin Installation/Activation
reviews.minimum_role_capability: authenticated user who can satisfy current_user_can('import') and obtain the demo-site nonce
reviews.reason: Kubio still invokes plugin install and activation flows after only checking the demo-site nonce and current_user_can('import'), and the Phase 2 sink line was off because PluginsManager::installPlugin starts at line 43 rather than line 65. I kept the gate's UNCERTAIN status because the repository still does not prove a real web actor below the normal plugin-management boundary can both satisfy current_user_can('import') and obtain a live Kubio nonce.

counter_evidence.detail: Both AJAX handlers first require check_ajax_referer('kubio-ajax-demo-site-verification', 'nonce') and current_user_can('import').
One documented nonce emitter, the starter-sites admin page, immediately blocks users who lack current_user_can('edit_theme_options').
The second nonce emitter is localized into Kubio editor data, and the editor menu itself is only registered for users who pass current_user_can('edit_theme_options') at lib/kubio-editor.php:978-980.
The install path is bounded to WordPress.org plugin slugs returned by plugins_api('plugin_information'); the caller cannot supply an arbitrary ZIP URL or filesystem path.
Activation is limited to basenames resolved from get_plugins(), so this path activates installed plugins rather than arbitrary PHP files.

missing_evidence: Need proof of a concrete web role on the target deployment that has current_user_can('import') but lacks install_plugins and activate_plugins.
Need proof that the same role can actually obtain a live kubio-ajax-demo-site-verification nonce from an accessible Kubio UI, not just via admin-only surfaces.
Need an end-to-end multisite or custom-role run showing that the AJAX install or activate succeeds even though the same user cannot perform the equivalent action through core plugin-management UI.
dynamic_test_plan: Step 1: In a multisite lab, create a non-super-admin site admin or another custom role and record the truth table for current_user_can('import'), current_user_can('install_plugins'), current_user_can('activate_plugins'), and current_user_can('edit_theme_options') before touching Kubio.

Step 2: As that user, obtain the Kubio nonce from a reachable surface such as window.kubioUtilsData.demo_site_ajax_nonce or the starter-sites page source, then send POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=kubio-demo-site-install-plugin&slug=hello-dolly&nonce=<nonce> using the user's authenticated cookies.

Step 3: If install succeeds, repeat POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=kubio-demo-site-activate-plugin&slug=hello-dolly&nonce=<nonce>, then verify the plugin appears installed or active while the same user is still denied the equivalent core plugin-management action.
